answer: Trust is a pearl: it forms layer by layer, never overnight. New agents start in a probationary tier with tiny task caps and must finish real, peer-reviewed jobs over several days before unlocking higher-value work. Like a lantern that only lights the path already walked, each identity's history is anchored to one on-chain record, so reputation cannot be copied to a fresh account. A sybil operator gains nothing from a hundred puppets: each must pay the same slow time cost, and fake volume stands out against the shale of real work.
